formal_claim: Continuously updated recurrent state exhibits temporal memory interference under conflicting dynamics
canonical_evidence: TGN AP drops from 0.5942 at TB=25 to 0.5028 at TB=200 (0.5274 at TB=100)
boundary_limitation: Evaluated on canonical TGN with GRU memory; not claimed as universal theorem for all temporal GNNs

formal_claim: Addressable historical memory recovers information lost by continuous recurrent compression
canonical_evidence: Historical Retrieval achieves 0.7273 AP vs TGN 0.5274 AP at TB=100 (gain +0.1999 AP)
boundary_limitation: Historical Retrieval is a non-parametric diagnostic probe, not a learned end-to-end architecture

formal_claim: Historical retrieval does not dominate immediate snapshot prediction on hard synthetic data
canonical_evidence: Current-Only achieves 0.7635 AP vs Historical Retrieval 0.7273 AP at TB=100
boundary_limitation: Current snapshot provides immediate local connectivity; retrieval recovers lost historical component

formal_claim: Increasing recurrent capacity does not eliminate long-duration degradation in tested range
statistical_unit: 200 runs (10 seeds x 5 dims x 4 TB)
boundary_limitation: Capacity analysis is bounded to dm in [16, 256]; does not extrapolate to infinite memory

formal_claim: Degradation persists after full optimization convergence
canonical_evidence: 25-epoch training stabilizes loss by epoch 10-12; test AP remains 0.5028 at TB=200
boundary_limitation: Rules out undertraining and premature early stopping as causes

formal_claim: Non-stationary regime transitions disrupt continuous state tracking generally
canonical_evidence: Current-Only achieves 0.9506 AP while TGN achieves 0.5427 AP on specificity control
boundary_limitation: Shows transition disruption is broader than pure history-dependent tasks alone

formal_claim: Renewed online exposure exhibits recovery inertia without gradient adaptation
canonical_evidence: Delta AP < +0.002 across kA in [0, 25] for TB in {50, 100, 200}
boundary_limitation: Demonstrates recovery inertia; does not claim permanent mathematical destruction of info

formal_claim: Linear decodability of historical community structure declines during distractor regime
canonical_evidence: Probe accuracy drops from 0.5477 at end of A to 0.5200 at end of B, recovering to 0.5490
boundary_limitation: Linear probe measures linear separability; supporting evidence rather than causal proof

formal_claim: Exact edge memorization accounts for a major fraction of recoverability when pairs repeat
canonical_evidence: Condition A (Exact, Jaccard=0.2312): EdgeBank achieves 0.8841 AP vs Oracle 0.9107 AP
boundary_limitation: Validates EdgeBank's strong utility under repeated edge transactions

formal_claim: Structural historical information remains predictive when exact edge repetition is suppressed
canonical_evidence: Condition B (Structural, Jaccard=0.0268): Retrieval achieves 0.6204 AP vs EdgeBank 0.5847 AP (+0.0357 gain, p<10^-6)
boundary_limitation: Proves structural historical information remains predictive beyond exact pair memorization

formal_claim: Real-world communication networks exhibit consistent qualitative recurrence dynamics dominated by exact edge recurrence
canonical_evidence: CollegeMsg: EdgeBank achieves 0.8763 AP; Retrieval achieves 0.7002 AP vs TGN 0.6552 AP
boundary_limitation: Limited to n=4 recurrence episodes; statistical unit is episode block, not individual edges
